analysis:
Documentation-only change to docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md. The complete range map covers base 536-562 and 623, and head 536-583 and 644-645. The supplied head_text stops at line 455, so the changed head lines are visible only in the truncated patch excerpt (hunk @@ -533,33 +533,54 @@). Head lines 1-455 match the unchanged base content I examined.

The base text at lines 536-562 said pair Macs never auto-update: the cluster service runs with updates off and the operator runs `darkbloom update` by hand. The new text says pair Macs update themselves while `auto_update` is on and `DARKBLOOM_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` is unset. Every 30 minutes, at a slot fixed by the pairing's cluster ID, each Mac's cluster service asks the coordinator for the latest release, then downloads, verifies and stages it while serving. The rest of that text is not visible.

This documents new attack surface: an updater now runs inside the cluster service. It touches A-011 and A-017 (signed-artifact identity and qualification), T-013 and T-043 (a replaceable binary and rollback authority), T-054 (stale or unqualified builds), and the cluster-approval build pinning at head 146-168 and 178-186. The threat model has no cluster-update entry.

Unverified contracts for the next pass:
- What "verifies" covers: signature, CodeDirectory and downgrade protection.
- Whether both ranks swap atomically. Mixed builds would conflict with the keyed native worker rule at head 281-283 and the build-pinned approval rule at head 163-165.
- Whether the derived update slot leaks the cluster ID.
- How a failed update rolls back.
- Removed base line 623 ("A pair does not update itself") and the change at head 644-645.

No implementing source was supplied. I raise no concrete regression, but the uncertainty is material: the updater source and the remaining head lines 456-656 need review.
